Question: The inlet and outlet dimensions of the centrifugal fan need to match the pipe dimensions of the boiler and heating furnace. How to deal with the situation that the size of the air inlet and outlet does not match the existing duct system?
Answer: While matching free area is ideal for the intake and supply ducts, it’s not going to impact the operation unless the difference is significant. The blower is designed to handle a certain amount of static (resistance to airflow). If one or the other is too small, it simply increases the velocity of the air in that duct. The downside is when you increase velocity you increase air noise. Faster moving air whistles as it either enters or leaves the duct system. Also, your duct system is designed for a certain amount of built in velocity. This is so the air coming out the supplies has sufficient throw. Meaning how far the air coming out will flow in order to comfortably heat the environment. A main residential supply line has a designed velocity of around 600’pm. Ideal duct systems are designed at around .1 SP overall. As the static increases due to filter clogging or other interference, the blower can overcome around .5- to nearly 1” of static in most air handlers and furnaces. The best way to determine the airflow in your system is to measure the airflow. Either by measuring the static in the system or the air through each duct.

Question: Is it distilling water if you fill up a gallon jug and leave the lid off for a couple of days? People say it evaporates some bad stuff out of it.

A piece of waterproof material, a small stone and a cup and you have a water still. Dig a small hole around 8” deep, pee in the hole. Place a cup in the middle. Cover the hole with the waterproof plastic material and pile dirt around the edges. Place a small stone in the middle so it forms and upside down cone. Then wait an hour for the sun to evaporate the pee and when it condenses on the underside of the plastic material it will run down to the middle and drip into the cup. We had a lot of P2V5models and they were scheduled for de commissioning., They came up with a novel idea that ultimately cost the lives of many of my friends. We didn’t know why but our planes we painted army green. They were outfitted with aft mounted machine guns. They pulled a number of Norton Bomb sites out of mothballs and mounted them below the nose forward of the landing gear. The plane had other changes and when they were through it looked like this picture. this mission was still classified in 2001 when it was finally de classified. We were sworn to secrecy until then. Their losses were very high and in less than a year they were de commissioned. I think of them often. I had the privilege of being given an honorary membership into their group which met every year in Vegas as a reunion.
